page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It includes 154 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between high memory capacity and limited compute performance. The single physical core architecture results in poor multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 1847.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1505.0. Single-core CPU performance is also modest, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1405.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1242.0. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with uncached read and write speeds of approximately 12.6 GB/sec, though cached small-block reads reach 85.83 GB/sec. Database and web serving operations are similarly limited, with Redis SET operations executing at 1.63 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 2.42 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4-2ds_v4 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads that require a large memory footprint but have low CPU demands. The inclusion of 154 GB of local storage and Premium Storage capability supports data-intensive operations. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, and basic data processing tasks that fit within the 32.0 GB memory limit but do not require intensive parallel processing.
